title: Parse-time error message publication

scope.rationale: sqlite3ErrorMsg is the shared parse-time error state transition. The native owner accepts already formatted typed bytes and centralizes parser identity assertions, byte-offset normalization, connection allocation, suppression, OOM, previous-message replacement, result code, and WITH-state cleanup. Expression analysis now consumes it instead of duplicating partial state updates.
excluded_responsibilities: C varargs decoding and sqlite3VMPrintf format rendering
Transfer of the final Parse error into the public connection after prepare
Migration of every remaining legacy inline Parse error writer

external_source_responsibilities: Typed callers render any format arguments before publication
Connection-aware allocator owns OOM fault propagation and lookaside/heap selection
Prepare completion transfers Parse state to the public connection
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete post-formatting source state transition is assigned. Multiple expression-analysis error paths invoke the shared owner; other inline legacy writers remain explicit migration work rather than part of this unit.

inputs: Active Parse owned by db.pParse or its pToplevel and already formatted borrowed message bytes
outputs: Updated Parse error count, result, owned message, WITH state, and normalized connection error byte offset
contracts.ownership: The connection allocator duplicates message bytes. An old Parse message is freed on publication; a suppressed new message is freed immediately.
contracts.state_and_results: Formatting begins with errByteOffset -2 and normalizes it to -1 when no formatter-specific offset is published. Suppressed ordinary errors do not alter Parse. Suppressed OOM increments nErr and sets NOMEM. Unsuppressed errors increment nErr, replace zErrMsg, set ERROR, and clear pWith.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: No I/O or callbacks. The caller owns connection/parser synchronization.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Allocation failure is recorded by the connection allocator. The function still follows the exact suppression or ordinary publication branch and leaves all message pointers owned or null.

representation_differences: Typed message slices replace C varargs. Formatting responsibility ends at the caller, while all post-format source state and ownership remain in this owner.
unreachable plus std.debug.assert represent non-null active database/parser invariants.
Connection allocator stringNDuplicate replaces sqlite3VMPrintf allocation after formatting.

oracle.protocol: Publish one message and verify ERROR/count/offset/text, replace it and verify ownership/count, enable suppression and verify the existing message and count remain unchanged, then inject allocation failure and compare suppression/OOM state.
oracle.normalization: Compare exact scalar state and message bytes after formatting.

assurance.oom: Connection-aware allocation records mallocFailed; suppression and ordinary publication branches preserve source error-count/result behavior.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O; Parse is connection-local and caller-synchronized.
assurance.malformed_input: Typed non-null Parse and bounded message slice; active parser identity is asserted.
assurance.continuation: Repeated errors replace old owned text safely; suppressed errors preserve the prior visible error.
assurance.performance: One message allocation and at most one old-message free per unsuppressed error.

integration.native_call_path: Expression analysis row-value, variable-limit, and expression-shape failures invoke setExpressionError, which delegates to parse_error.report.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: The expression-analysis helper's partial free/duplicate/count/result implementation is retired in favor of the complete shared state owner.

independent_review.notes: Requires formatter-boundary and OOM differential, broader call-site migration, assurance closure, and independent review.

known_blockers: Migrate remaining inline Parse error writers to the shared owner where source identity applies.
Add maintained pinned-C suppression, replacement, offset, and allocation-failure differential trace.
